//: Discussion on how to write comments in package.json:
name: wacz-signer
description: Local wacz-auth signing stand-in — a private CA, an RFC 3161 timestamp authority, and a signer, all driven by openssl.
//bin: The CLI. Points at dist/, so `pnpm run build` has to have run — test/cli.test.ts builds first for exactly this reason.
//files: dist/ only. LICENSE, package.json and README.md are included automatically.
NOTICE is not, and does not need to be: the MIT-licensed fixtures it covers live
in test/fixtures/, which is not published either — so no py-wacz material ships.

//scripts.build: Compile src/ to dist/ via tsconfig.build.json (which excludes test/). dist/cli.js is what `bin` points at, so this is what ships — test/cli.test.ts spawns it rather than importing the source, and would otherwise measure whatever dist/ happened to hold.
//scripts.typecheck: Type-check everything including test/, without emitting. Separate from `build` because the build deliberately narrows to src/.
//scripts.test: Vitest, single run. The safeguard against a round trip that agrees with itself about the wrong format is not test ordering — it is that verify-real-fixtures checks the verifier against py-wacz's signed archives, an oracle this package did not produce. (An earlier version of this note claimed the files were deliberately ordered; no such mechanism was ever configured, and the tests are independent, so order buys nothing.)
//scripts.lint: ESLint with zero tolerance for warnings. --max-warnings 0 so a warning cannot accumulate into background noise.
//scripts.site:dev: Astro dev server for docs-site/. npm, not pnpm: docs-site is a separate npm project with its own lockfile (same split as BrowserHive).
//scripts.site:build: Build docs-site/ to docs-site/dist/. NOT a drift guard on its own — see site:check.
//scripts.site:check: site:build plus scripts/check-doc-refs.mjs. Use this, not site:build, when you want the guarantee: a missing `// #region` only fails the build on .mdx pages, and every page here is .md, where Starlight's loader catches the error and still exits 0. check-doc-refs.mjs is the part that exits non-zero. CI runs this.
//scripts.audit: Known-vulnerability gate for both lockfiles: pnpm-lock.yaml (pnpm audit) and docs-site/package-lock.json (npm audit — pnpm audit never reads it). --audit-level=low, so the only passing count is zero. Needs no install: both commands read the lockfiles. CI runs it from .github/workflows/audit.yml on pull requests, pushes, daily and on demand. On 2026-09-13 vitest carried a moderate advisory and the docs-site lockfile four more (astro's critical one among them) while Dependabot alerts sat open and nothing was red. Fix by advancing the lockfile (pnpm update <pkg> --recursive --depth Infinity, npm audit fix), not with an override that leaves it where it is. Only an advisory with no fixed release may be skipped with --ignore <GHSA>, next to a note saying why and when to remove it.
//scripts.check: audit + typecheck + lint + test: what to run before pushing. CI runs the same pieces, but audit lives in its own workflow (audit.yml) because advisories are published between pull requests, so it also runs daily.

scripts.check: pnpm run audit && pnpm run typecheck && pnpm run lint && pnpm test

author: Takahito Urai

//devDependencies.@eslint/js: ESLint's own recommended rule set, consumed by eslint.config.mjs.
//devDependencies.@types/node: Node type definitions. wacz-signer is Node-only — there is no browser code here.
//devDependencies.eslint: Linter. Flat config in eslint.config.mjs, shared in shape with the sibling repositories.
//devDependencies.eslint-import-resolver-typescript: Lets import-x resolve TypeScript path/extension conventions — notably the .js specifiers that ESM TypeScript writes for .ts files.
//devDependencies.eslint-plugin-import-x: Import hygiene: enforces the .js extension on relative imports, which Node's ESM resolver requires at runtime. Pulls in unrs-resolver, whose native build must be allowed in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
//devDependencies.typescript: The compiler. Also the type gate: `typecheck` covers test/, `build` narrows to src/.
//devDependencies.typescript-eslint: The typescript-eslint preset bundle (parser + plugin + configs). eslint.config.mjs turns on strictTypeChecked and stylisticTypeChecked from it, which is why linting needs a tsconfig and is slower than a syntax-only pass.
//devDependencies.vitest: Test runner. Pulls in esbuild, whose platform binary is installed by a postinstall — allowed explicitly in pnpm-workspace.yaml, since pnpm 11 runs no dependency lifecycle scripts by default.

//dependencies: One, and it is not a cryptographic one.
wacz-signer does no cryptography of its own: key generation, certificates, digests,
signatures and RFC 3161 are all openssl invocations, and this package supplies
the JSON, the temp files and the process handling around them. So the thing it
really needs at run time is the openssl CLI, which comes from the system (or
apt, in the Dockerfile — node:24-bookworm-slim does not ship it).
commander parses the command line, and is imported by src/cli.ts alone. The
parser it replaced was hand-rolled and dropped unknown flags in silence, so a
mistyped --signer-days left an identity meant to be expired valid instead.
//packageManager: Read by pnpm/action-setup@v4 in CI, so the version there matches this one without being repeated in the workflow. See pnpm-workspace.yaml for the two places pnpm departs from npm silently (allowBuilds, enablePrePostScripts).
//engines: Node 24 for the ESM and type-stripping era the sibling repositories target. .nvmrc carries the same number for CI.
